newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Monday with early-maturing contracts continuing an upward trend while later-maturing contracts were down on profit-taking, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,335 yuan ($402) per tonne, losing 14 yuan. It opened at 3,340 and hit a high of 3,347.
March did not trade, May rose 82 yuan to 3,420, July 25 to 3,430, November fell 14 to 3,345 and the January 1998 contract 17 to 3,352.
Combined volume fell to 23,700 tonnes from 26,200.

"Early-maturing contracts rose today on speculative buying, given price gains on the spot soybean market," one trader said. "But later-maturing contracts met strong selling pressure, with investors uncertain about the medium trend on the spot market."
Traders said volume had not risen despite the price gains of the past few days, which had reduced the confidence of long position holders.
Analysts said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the short term.
